Lesson · 20 min

Transitions, Animations, and Speaker Notes

Add slide transitions and object animations in the Motion panel, control when animations start, and write speaker notes for whoever presents.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Add a transition to one slide or to every slide
  • ✓Animate an object, choose when the animation starts, and play it back
  • ✓Show the speaker notes area and write notes for the presenter
  • ✓Use motion so it helps the audience instead of distracting them

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Motion with a purpose

On the job

The welcome presentation will run two ways.

On the lobby screen, the slides play by themselves, so bullet points can't wait for a click. At tenant orientation, Denise presents it and wants reminders of what to hand out and say. Both need gentle motion, not spinning text.

Your task: Add a transition, animate the first-week list, and write speaker notes.

Add a transition

  1. Select the slide in the filmstrip.
  2. Select Slide › Transition. The Motion panel opens on the right.
  3. Under Slide transition, choose a transition, such as Dissolve. Drag the speed slider to make it faster or slower.
  4. To use the same transition everywhere, select Apply to all slides.
  5. Select Play to preview it.

Animate an object

  1. Select the object on the slide, such as the bulleted text.
  2. Select Insert › Animation (or View › Motion) to open the Motion panel. If no animation is listed for the object under Object Animations, select Add animation. New object animations are set to Appear (On click) by default.
  3. Choose the animation you want from the drop-down, such as Fade in.
  4. Choose when it starts: On click, After previous, or With previous. For text, check By paragraph to bring in one bullet at a time.
  5. Drag the speed slider if needed, and select Play to preview.
Drag and drop: match

When should it start?

Drag the right start option onto each situation.

Drag each card into place, or tap a card and then tap where it goes.

Denise wants each bullet to appear only when she's ready to talk about it

💡 Use one or two kinds of motion for the whole presentation. If every slide spins, bounces, and flies, people watch the motion instead of reading the message.

Speaker notes

Speaker notes sit under each slide. They're for the presenter: reminders, details, and what to hand out. The audience doesn't see them during the slideshow. If the notes area is hidden, choose View › Show speaker notes, then click in it (it says Click to add speaker notes) and type.

Worked example

Notes for the First Week slide

Help whoever presents the welcome presentation cover everything on slide 2.

  1. 1

    Keep the slide short: three bullet points.

    Tenants read the slide; the presenter adds the details.

  2. 2

    In the notes, write “Hand out the key fob form here.”

    It's an action for the presenter, not something tenants need to read on screen.

  3. 3

    Add the office phone hours to the notes.

    If someone asks, the presenter has the answer without adding clutter to the slide.

Result: A clean slide for the audience, and a script for the presenter.

🔑 Put what the audience must see on the slide; put what the presenter must say or do in the notes.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

In your own practice presentation:

  1. Add a transition to one slide, then select Apply to all slides.
  2. Animate the text on one slide with Fade in, By paragraph, starting On click. Play it.
  3. Write a speaker note on at least two slides.
  4. Start the slideshow and click through the animated slide to check the timing.
Deliverable: Submit a screenshot showing the Motion panel and a slide with speaker notes to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Google Slides, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
